 Moore benefits from break but fitness remains unclear
 Wrexham AFC 
 Football 
 Sport 
 By 
 Nick Harrison
 Share
 0 Comments 
 Wrexham's Kieffer Moore (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire) 
 This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today,
 and has been written by our American colleagues.
 It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.
 PHIL PARKINSON says Kieffer Moore benefited from the international break but stopped short of confirming whether the striker would be fit to face Lincoln City on Saturday.
 The Wrexham boss also urged patience with forwards Josh Windass, Callum O’Hare and Nathan Broadhead as the trio work their way back from injury.
 Moore missed Wales duty after a scan showed that an issue in his back was affecting his hamstring.
 Wrexham shared the scan with the Welsh FA, and Parkinson said the decision to give the striker time to recover had helped.
 “He needed a week or so to get that right and, you know, we feel it’s been beneficial for him,” said Parkinson.
 Parkinson said Windass, O’Hare and Broadhead were progressing, though “maybe not to the levels we first hoped”.
 On Windass, he said: “We want to make sure that ankle is 100 per cent before we expose him again to training and first-team football because he’s an important player.”
 Parkinson gave no return date for any of the three, saying the club had to make decisions with “the next few months in mind” rather than rushing players back.
